standing: THIS FILE IS THE STANDARD. It is the cosyte estate's engineering baseline and it inherits its authority from no other document: there is no prose twin, and by operator decision none is to be written. Every requirement below carries its own provenance note saying where it was derived from, so no requirement is inherited unexamined. scripts/drift-check.js evaluates it and prints a per-repo WORKLIST; scripts/validate-drift-manifest.mjs validates this file against drift-manifest.schema.json, which ships beside it and needs no install to run. THE AUTHOR IS A SUBJECT TOO: configSubject below states which of these requirements config itself is held to and which it is exempt from, so the repo that publishes the standard is graded by it rather than standing outside it. AND NO ADVISORY RANGE IS TRANSCRIBED HERE: an override cites advisory IDENTIFIERS, and the ranges are read from the advisory record at check time, because a transcribed range decays silently while the sentence beside it still reads true. Drift is EXPECTED while the migration runs: the report is the worklist, never a claim of health.

estate.provenance: The umbrella's .gitmodules is the list of record for repo names, PATHS and hazards. These are its 24 submodule PATHS as of 2026-08-29, read for S0226. Repos are addressed by PATH and never by submodule NAME: the org profile repo is NAMED `.github` and PATHED `github-profile`, and since the checker resolves a repo by joining the umbrella root with the name it is given, and the umbrella root has its own `.github/` directory, addressing that repo by name would silently grade the umbrella's own workflows.

package.title: The 13 @cosyte/* package repos
package.provenance: The same thirteen the pre-change manifest named as `targets`, re-derived rather than inherited: documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md measured every one of them as a published-or-publishable npm package consuming five or six of the shared @cosyte/* config packages, and scripts/parser-template/ in this checkout is the scaffold they are generated from, so what a package repo owes can be read off a tree that exists here. The operator decision (documentation/decisions/operator-decision-shared-utilities-s0047.md, `The baseline`) directed that this baseline be re-derived AND extended beyond build config.

toolchain.provenance: Carried unchanged from manifest version 1 and re-derived against documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md, which measured `pnpm@10` across all thirteen (fhir pins the full sha512 form, which satisfies a prefix rule and is recorded there as a weaker guarantee rather than a violation) and Node >= 22 as the estate floor. scripts/parser-template/package.json, the scaffold every parser is born from, ships `packageManager: pnpm@10.0.0` and `engines.node: >=22.0.0`.

sharedConfig.provenance: Carried unchanged from manifest version 1. documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md measured every package sampled (hl7, x12, dicom, deid, cli) as depending on five or six of the published @cosyte/* config packages, and named the five below as the published-and-in-use set. scripts/parser-template/package.json declares `prettier: @cosyte/prettier-config` and scripts/parser-template/tsconfig.json extends `@cosyte/tsconfig/base.json`.

scripts.provenance: Carried unchanged from manifest version 1 and re-derived against scripts/parser-template/package.json in this checkout, which declares every one of these thirteen script names and lints at `--max-warnings=0`. The scaffold is the derivation: a name required here that the scaffold does not create would be a requirement no new parser repo could satisfy on the day it is born.

dependencies.provenance: devDepVersions and caretAllowed carried unchanged from manifest version 1; scripts/parser-template/package.json carries the override block, which is where a new repo inherits it. caretAllowedScopes states what the checker used to hardcode: a workspace-internal @cosyte/* dependency may stay on a caret range. THE OVERRIDES ARE DEPENDABOT DEV/BUILD-TIME ADVISORY REMEDIATION, AND EACH ONE NOW CITES ITS ADVISORY IN pnpmOverrideAdvisories RATHER THAN IN PROSE. Version 1 argued from a sentence in `pnpmOverridesComment` that named advisories in English beside hand-transcribed ranges, and the transcription decayed: the pin sat at a version the advisory it argued from had already superseded, config's own manifest disagreed with this one, and nothing compared them. What survives here is the reachability argument, which no advisory record can supply. esbuild: a dev-server path traversal, not reachable, since these repos build via tsup/vitest and never run `esbuild serve`. js-yaml: a quadratic merge-key DoS and a prototype-pollution issue, reached at BUILD and RELEASE time only, over YAML this estate wrote itself. THE 3.x REACH IS NO LONGER A RESIDUAL: js-yaml 3.14.2 arrives through read-yaml-file@1.1.0 (@manypkg/get-packages, @changesets/cli) and calls yaml.safeLoad, which js-yaml 4 removed, so version 1 recorded the branch as not pinnable and left it un-remediated. That reasoning applied to the 4.x MAJOR, never to the 3.x branch: 3.x still ships safeLoad, so the branch is pinned on its own line and the release tooling keeps the API it calls. Which version each advisory first patches is NOT written here; the checker reads it from the advisory at check time and fails an override pinned below it.

ciWorkflows.provenance: EXTENDED here, and the extension is measured rather than chosen. The operator decision puts `the CI workflow baseline` in scope. documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md measured the common core across the thirteen packages as ci, codeql, no-emdash, no-internal-refs, release and scorecard, and recorded exactly two gaps in it: dicom carries no no-internal-refs, deid carries no no-emdash. Manifest version 1 required only the four that scripts/parser-template/.github/workflows ships (ci, codeql, release, scorecard), so those two gaps were invisible to the checker. Requiring all six is what puts them on the worklist. Filenames follow the measured convention that each repo's workflow is a thin caller named after the reusable workflow it calls.

phiScan.provenance: PHI scan is in scope by the operator's own words in the decision (`PHI SCAN, etc`). The three required files are measured: documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md records that all 13 packages reference the shared pipeline's PHI-scan step and all 13 carry phi-scan-overrides.md, and that hl7, dicom and deid each ship their own scripts/phi-scan.ts and scripts/phi-allow-list.txt; scripts/parser-template/ scaffolds all three. The capability probe is carried unchanged from manifest version 1, parameters and all: it RUNS each repo's scanner against a synthetic corpus rather than matching its source, and its own controls gate the entire report. Publishing the scanner as a shared package is a separate component item and is NOT required here.

releaseTooling.provenance: NEW in manifest version 2; `release tooling` is named in the operator decision's Scope. Every requirement is read off scripts/parser-template/ in this checkout, which is the tree every parser repo is generated from: its package.json declares the `changeset` and `release` scripts, `publishConfig.access: public` and `publishConfig.provenance: true`, and `@changesets/cli` as a devDependency, and it ships .changeset/config.json with `access: public` and `baseBranch: main`. `prepublishOnly` is required by the scripts group and is not restated. release.yml is required by the ciWorkflows group and is not restated either.

agentDoc.provenance: NEW in manifest version 2, and SHAPE ONLY. The operator overturned decision 15 for shape alone on 2026-08-29 (documentation/decisions/operator-decision-shared-utilities-s0047.md, `Decision 15 is OVERTURNED, for SHAPE only`): the umbrella may standardize required sections and a line budget and NEVER content. documentation/documentation-standard.md row 16 already names this manifest as where that shape is defined and drift-check as its enforcer. The filename and the five headings are taken from scripts/parser-template/CLAUDE.md, the scaffold every parser repo is born from and the only agent-context doc this checkout can read: the research doc's `What was NOT checked` records that no repo's own AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md was read, so nothing here is derived from one. AGENTS.md is accepted as an alternative filename because documentation/documentation-standard.md names both. The line budget is a DECLARED ceiling rather than a measurement: the scaffold is 166 lines, and 300 is that with headroom. A heading matches when the file carries a heading line that STARTS WITH the declared text, so a repo may qualify its own headings without failing the shape.

light.title: The 11 repos that cannot share a build config
light.provenance: The authorizing decision asks for `A SECOND, LIGHTER baseline for the other 11 repos` and then names TEN of them (crew, pathways, website, iac, docs, knowledgebase, assets, claude-containers, github-profile, dates). The COUNT is right and the LIST is one short. Resolved against .gitmodules, the list of record: 24 submodules, minus the 13 package repos, minus those ten, leaves exactly one repo unaccounted for, `config` ITSELF. So CONFIG IS THE ELEVENTH LIGHT REPO: counted by the decision, not named by it. config is a pnpm workspace but has never been one of the 13 package targets, and the decision explicitly REFUSED both `one baseline for all 24 repos` and `only the 13 with the rest excluded`, which only adds up if the two baselines together cover all 24. documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md independently records config as an outlier on exactly the axes this baseline covers: no codeql, no no-internal-refs, no scorecard. If the operator intended config to be exempt from BOTH baselines, the reversal is one entry here and one line in estate.submodulePaths.
light.ceiling: Exactly three groups: the em-dash gate, ONE CI entry point, and the security workflows. The decision's words are `A Terraform repo and a parser cannot share a build config; they can share no-emdash, a CI entry point and the security workflows`, and nothing else may be added to this baseline without a new operator decision. In particular no build, lint, format, dependency or agent-doc requirement belongs here.

emdashGate.provenance: The decision names no-emdash as one of the three things these repos can share. documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md measured pathways and claude-containers as already carrying a `no-emdash` workflow, so the requirement describes something two of these repos already do. The requirement is the WORKFLOW rather than a package script because most repos in this baseline carry no package.json at all, and a requirement they cannot express is a requirement that only ever reports drift.

ciEntryPoint.provenance: The decision names `a CI entry point`. The NAME is derived rather than invented: documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md records that each repo's workflow is a thin CALLER of the reusable workflow in cosyte/.github (hl7's ci.yml is `uses: cosyte/.github/.github/workflows/ci.yml@main`), and ci.yml is what the package baseline and scripts/parser-template/.github/workflows already require. Measured today, this is a WORKLIST entry for most of these repos rather than a description of them: crew carries `lint` only, assets `pr-check`, knowledgebase `format`, and dates NO workflows at all. Wiring dates is explicitly the first task of S0188 by the same decision, not of this item.

securityWorkflows.provenance: The decision names `the security workflows`. WHICH two they are is read off the package baseline and the scaffold rather than assumed: scripts/parser-template/.github/workflows ships codeql.yml and scorecard.yml, and manifest version 1 already required both of the thirteen. documentation/research/shared-utilities-current-state.md measures config itself as carrying NEITHER, which is one of the three drifts that put config in this baseline.

phiScanProbeComment: Parameters for the one BEHAVIOURAL check in scripts/drift-check.js: it RUNS each repo's scripts/phi-scan.ts against a throwaway corpus and asks whether it refuses over a target it enumerated and never read. THE MACHINERY NOW LIVES IN @cosyte/script-utils/phi-scan, so the probe PLANTS that package into the throwaway repository before running, and WHICH copy it plants is the adoption check: the controls plant config's own working copy, a target repo is graded against the version THAT repo has installed, and a repo that has not adopted carries a self-contained scanner and needs nothing planted. A repo that HAS adopted but has no node_modules yields a scanner that cannot start, prints no marker, and lands on `inconclusive` rather than on a pass. It is a capability probe, never a regex over the scanner's source: this class has produced six defects that lived in a prose carrier while the code was right, so matching prose would grade the comment. NOTHING HERE NAMES AN EXIT CODE, deliberately. The siblings do not agree on their codes, so the probe derives each repo's HITS code from a control run and treats only exit 0 as `reported clean`. A perRepo entry exists for a repo whose scanner does not read the default fixture (dicom tiers by EXTENSION), and the probe answers `inconclusive` rather than passing when it cannot ground its own premise.

dicom.$why: dicom's text pass detects DICOM's own shapes (a PN token, a recent date), not a dashed SSN, so the default payload scanned CLEAN there and the probe answered `inconclusive` rather than passing. The payload below is a synthetic PN. Measured 2026-08-11.

configSubjectComment: WHY THE AUTHOR IS GRADED SEPARATELY, AND WHY NOT BY ADDING IT TO A `repos` LIST. `baselines.package.repos` is the roster of @cosyte/* PARSER repos: the phi-scan capability probe iterates it, and a repo named there is expected to carry scripts/phi-scan.ts, codeql.yml and thirteen package scripts. config carries none of those, so putting it there would print drift that is not drift and would corrupt what the roster means. `baselines.light` is the other side of the same coin: it says what config owes as one of the eleven repos that cannot share a build config, and its ceiling is set by an operator decision to exactly three groups. Neither answers the question this block exists for, which is what the repo that PUBLISHES the standard owes to the standard. So config is graded as its own subject, against the package baseline minus a NAMED exemption per rule that does not apply. The exemptions are the point: a rule config is silently not held to is indistinguishable from a rule config passes, and the checker refuses an exemption naming a rule the baseline does not carry, so this list cannot outlive the requirements it excuses.

configSubject.provenance: S0091-config-2, 2026-08-29. Derived by reading config's own package.json and working tree against every requirement kind baselines.package declares, one at a time: eleven of them are graded and config satisfies all eleven, and the nine below are excused with the reason each was excused for. Nothing here was inherited: the exempted set is what was left after grading, not a list chosen in advance. The baseline named is `package` because that is the estate's real standard; the light baseline still holds config for the workflow requirements an operator decision put there, and those are excused here rather than graded twice under two names.

exemptions.why: config PUBLISHES @cosyte/tsconfig; the workspace root compiles nothing of its own and carries no tsconfig.json to extend anything from. Each packages/* extends the base config itself, which is the requirement holding where there is source to compile.

The thirteen script names describe a published parser package. config's root manifest is a workspace ROOT: build, test, lint and typecheck delegate with `pnpm --filter ./packages/*`, and phi-scan, clean and prepublishOnly belong to a package that has a corpus to scan and a tarball to publish. Each packages/* is where the names are owed.

config's root `lint` script runs no linter; it delegates to the workspace packages. The --max-warnings=0 flag is owed where eslint is actually invoked, which is each packages/* lint script, and asserting it on a delegating script would grade the delegation.

The pinned toolchain describes a package that bundles, lints and type-checks its own source. config's root declares only what the workspace itself runs (vitest, tsup, prettier, typescript, all at the pinned majors) and deliberately declares no eslint, vite or attw, because the packages that need them declare them. Grading the root against the full set would report four drifts nothing could fix without adding dependencies this repo does not use.

config is held to the LIGHT baseline's workflow requirements (emdashGate, ciEntryPoint, securityWorkflows), which is where an operator decision put it. Grading the same .github/workflows directory twice would count one gap as two drifts under two names. The gaps that baseline reports today, codeql.yml and scorecard.yml, are real and are the worklist entry; they are owned by phase config#CONFIG-4, not excused here.

config hosts the shared PHI-scan engine (packages/script-utils/phi-scan.js) and the template scanner every parser repo is generated from. It has no scripts/phi-scan.ts, no allow-list and no corpus of its own, because it is the source of those files rather than a consumer of them.

The probe's own two controls already RUN config's engine, on every drift run, before any repo is graded, and the whole report is refused if either misbehaves. Grading config as a probe subject would run the same engine a third time with no scanner to point it at, and an inconclusive answer there would read as a config drift rather than as what it is.

The root manifest is `private: true` and publishes nothing, so it carries no publishConfig to grade. The eight published packages/* each declare publishConfig.access and provenance, and scripts/npm-config-allow.mjs pins both values for every one of them on the release path.

config carries no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md today. The overturned decision authorised a SHAPE rule for the thirteen package repos, and writing config's own agent doc is new prose rather than the transcription fix this slice is; deleting this entry is the single edit that puts config back on the rule, and until then the gap is stated here instead of being invisible.

reDerivation.provenance: S0226-config-drift-manifest, 2026-08-29. Manifest version 1 declared its own authority to be a prose document in the umbrella that had since been deleted, so every requirement in it was inherited from a file nobody could read. The operator decided to re-derive AND extend it, to add a second lighter baseline, and to write no prose companion. This record is what makes the re-derivation auditable: every top-level key version 1 carried is listed in preChangeKeys and accounted for in exactly one of the two lists below, so no requirement can vanish unmentioned.

droppedOrChanged.now: dropped; replaced by `standing` plus a per-group provenance note
droppedOrChanged.reason: It named an umbrella prose document as the authoritative source and called this file its machine-checkable shadow. That document no longer exists, so the claim made every requirement here unfalsifiable. The operator ruled that nothing replaces it and that this manifest IS the standard, so the authority claim is dropped rather than repointed, and provenance moves down to each group where it can be checked.

There are two baselines now, and a single flat list cannot say which one a repo is held to. The thirteen names are unchanged; only their location and the fact that the other eleven repos are now named as well have changed.

droppedOrChanged.now: split: the reachability argument survives in baselines.package.groups.dependencies.provenance, and the advisory CITATIONS moved to the machine-readable pnpmOverrideAdvisories
droppedOrChanged.reason: Every group carries a provenance note now, so a separate comment key beside one requirement is redundant. The re-derivation preserved this one verbatim, and preserving it kept the defect it carried: it named advisories in English beside hand-transcribed version ranges, nothing read it, and both the range and the pin it argued for had gone stale. The half no advisory record can supply, why the dev/build-time reach is not exploitable, is prose and stays prose. The half a record CAN supply, which advisory and what it first patches, is now an identifier the checker resolves at check time.

The re-derivation carried the VALUE unchanged, and the value was wrong: js-yaml was pinned at a version below the first patched version of the advisory the comment beside it argued from, and the 3.x branch was written off as not pinnable on a premise (safeLoad is gone) that is true of js-yaml 4 and false of the 3.x line the release tooling actually resolves. Both branches are now pinned on their own line, and the checker grades every pin against the advisory rather than against this file.

Version 1 required ci.yml, release.yml, codeql.yml and scorecard.yml, which is the set scripts/parser-template ships. The research doc measured the common core across the thirteen as six, including no-emdash and no-internal-refs, and measured exactly two repos as missing one each. Requiring four could never surface those two gaps, and surfacing them is what a worklist is for.

droppedOrChanged.was: checker rule, hardcoded in scripts/drift-check.js: a @cosyte/* devDependency may stay on a caret range
droppedOrChanged.reason: Behaviour is unchanged; the rule is now declared in the file that calls itself the standard instead of living only in the tool that reads it. A requirement nobody can find in the manifest is the failure this whole re-derivation exists to undo.

droppedOrChanged.was: checker rule, hardcoded in scripts/drift-check.js: a repo with no package.json is SKIPPED as greenfield
droppedOrChanged.now: baselines.<name>.missingPackageJson, `skip` for the package baseline and `evaluate` for the light one
droppedOrChanged.reason: Unchanged for the package baseline, where a repo with no package.json is genuinely greenfield. Applied unchanged to the light baseline it would have silently skipped nearly every repo in it, since most carry no package.json at all, and a baseline that skips its own members reports health it never measured.
